_units: abv %vol; sugar g per 100 ml (solids: % by mass); acid % titratable; dash = 0.8 ml; drop = 0.05 ml
_rules: Vetoes are medical: classify on the safe side (Robin 2026-09-24)
nutmeg, coconut, orgeat, amaretto, hazelnut liqueur, pine nuts -> nuts
undistilled beer/malt -> gluten; distilled grain spirits are NOT gluten
spice = heat only (bitters and baking spices are not spice)
wine fining agents ignored unless a named bottle is labelled

unknown ingredient -> the Mixologist adds it with scripts/add_ingredient.py, allergens on the safe side (every veto it could plausibly touch). His call, not Robin's: the guest's own veto protects them. The table follows the drink, never limits it (Robin 2026-09-25)

agave_nectar.name: agave nectar (straight)
agave_nectar.source: Liquid Intelligence p. 53: ~75% sugar by weight, dense; use ~60% of the simple-syrup volume, so ~100 g/100 ml sucrose-equivalent. Fructose tastes sweeter cold (p. 51)

lemongrass_syrup.name: lemongrass syrup (1:1)
lemongrass_syrup.source: 1:1 sugar syrup infused with lemongrass: sugar as LI simple syrup (pp. 136-137); lemongrass adds aroma only (Flavor Matrix pdf 164)

salt.name: kosher salt (for half the rim)
salt.source: plain sodium chloride; rimmed on the outside of half the glass (Codex p. 212 method), not modelled in balance

vanilla_syrup.name: vanilla syrup (1:1)
vanilla_syrup.source: 1:1 sugar syrup steeped with a split vanilla pod: sugar as LI simple syrup (pp. 136-137); vanilla adds aroma only

cherry_tomato.name: ripe cherry tomatoes, muddled and strained (juice)
cherry_tomato.source: unsourced standard value (ripe tomato ~3-4 g sugars/100 g, ~0.35-0.5% titratable acid as citric); no tomato row in LI's table (pp. 136-137)

tomato_vanilla_syrup.name: cherry-tomato and vanilla syrup (1:1 by weight, tomato juice and sugar)
tomato_vanilla_syrup.source: derived: 100 g strained ripe cherry-tomato juice (cherry_tomato row, unsourced standard value) + 100 g sugar ~ 162 ml (LI simple-syrup density, pp. 136-137) -> 63.9 g sugar/100 ml, 0.28% acid; vanilla pod adds aroma only

creme_de_noyaux.name: crème de noyaux (apricot-kernel liqueur)
creme_de_noyaux.source: unsourced standard value (~30% ABV, sugar assumed like maraschino, LI pp. 136-137); made from apricot/peach kernels, almond-flavoured: nuts on the safe side, same call as amaretto/maraschino

egg_yolk.name: egg yolk (one large, raw)
egg_yolk.source: unsourced standard value (~17 ml per large yolk, negligible sugar/acid); raw egg: the veto enum's only egg entry is 'egg-white', so a yolk counts there on the safe side

cherry_tomato_whole.name: cherry tomato (whole, garnish)
cherry_tomato_whole.source: garnish only: one small ripe cherry tomato, slit and sat on the rim; not in the balance

cranberry_syrup.name: cranberry syrup (1:1 by weight, unsweetened 100% cranberry juice and sugar, stirred cold)
cranberry_syrup.source: derived: 100 g unsweetened 100% cranberry juice (unsourced standard value: ~4 g sugars/100 g, ~2.4% titratable acid as citric) + 100 g sugar ~ 162 ml (LI simple-syrup density, pp. 136-137) -> 64.2 g sugar/100 ml, 1.48% acid. Not cranberry cocktail (Codex p. 183)

caramel_shard.name: dark caramel shard (sugar cooked dry to dark amber, set thin on baking paper, broken)
caramel_shard.source: derived: sucrose cooked to dark amber, modelled as sucrose by mass; caramelised sugar tastes less sweet than sucrose (Liquid Intelligence pdf 187) and loses a little mass in cooking, so the printed sugar overstates the sweetness a guest tastes

absinthe_lucid.name: Lucid Absinthe Supérieure (62%)
absinthe_lucid.source: label: 62% ABV (124 US proof), grande wormwood, fennel, sweet anise; Hester, fact card ted-breaux-absinthe F15 (Wikipedia citing the 2007 label approval + a specialist retailer). Unsweetened, as absinthe verte

tamarind_water.name: tamarind water (100 g sour seedless tamarind pulp block soaked in 250 ml hot water, pressed through a sieve)
tamarind_water.source: Hester's tamarind fact card (El-Siddig et al. 2006, secondary): dried pulp 8-18% tartaric (about half bound as cream of tartar, not sour) and 25-45% sugars; at 100 g : 250 ml, total acid 2.3-5.1%, sour part ~half; sugar 7-13 g/100. F5: a 20-24% pulp drink syrup ~1.11% total acidity. Row uses the middle of the sour range (2.0%) and of sugar (10). Sour block only (sweet Thai 2-3%). Revised by Tomás round 4 (was 20 g / 4.0%, an overestimate).

vodka_citrus.name: citrus vodka (lemon-flavoured, unsweetened, e.g. Absolut Citron style)
vodka_citrus.source: unsourced standard value: flavoured vodkas of the Citron style are bottled at 40% and read as unsweetened; if a bottle is sweetened, sugar is understated

cranberry_juice_unsweetened.name: unsweetened 100% cranberry juice (bottled, 'just cranberry')
cranberry_juice_unsweetened.source: unsourced standard value (same basis as cranberry_syrup's juice: ~4 g sugars/100 g, ~2.4% titratable acid as citric). Codex p. 183: 'very tannic'

cranberry_cocktail.name: cranberry juice cocktail (sweetened, ~27% juice)
cranberry_cocktail.source: unsourced estimate: ~30 g sugars per 240 ml label serving; acid = 27% of unsweetened juice's 2.4%. For the 'before' comparison only

rum_aged_tea.name: aged rum steeped with black tea (about 30 g loose black tea per litre, 20-40 minutes, strained)
rum_aged_tea.source: method after LI p. 268-269 (Arnold's tea vodka: 32 g tea per 1 L, 20-40 min, 'go dark'); tea adds no measurable sugar or acid; a little rum is lost in the leaves, ABV change ignored

basil_leaf.name: fresh basil leaf (sweet/Genovese basil)
basil_leaf.source: herb leaf, shaken with the drink for aroma and fine-strained out; not modelled in balance. Pairing: Flavor Matrix, Berry (pdf 52: basil a surprise pairing for berries incl. cranberry) and Kiwi (pdf 156: basil and vaccinium both surprise pairings)

green_olive_brine.name: green olive brine (from plain, unstuffed green olives in brine)
green_olive_brine.source: unsourced standard value: brine of salt, water and a little lactic acid/vinegar; salt ~8% not modelled; dosed by the dash as a seasoning

passion_fruit_syrup.name: passion fruit syrup (1:1 by weight, fresh or bottled juice and sugar)
passion_fruit_syrup.source: unsourced standard value: 1:1 juice:sugar by weight; passion fruit juice ~3.5% acid (citric), halved; sugar as a 1:1 syrup

lime_caraway_cordial.name: lime and caraway cordial (150 ml fresh lime juice, 90 g sugar, 90 ml water, zest of 4 limes, 1 tsp caraway seeds; warmed until the sugar dissolves, never boiled, steeped 20 min off the heat, strained; about 300 ml, fridge)
lime_caraway_cordial.source: computed from its recipe with LI table values (lime juice 1.6 g/100 ml sugar, 6.0% acid; 0.62 ml per g dissolved sugar): 92.4 g sugar and 9 g acid in ~296 ml. Zest and caraway carry aroma only. Unsourced: evaporation while warming (ignored; brief, below a simmer).

ginger_beer.name: ginger beer (commercial, sweetened, non-alcoholic)
ginger_beer.source: unsourced standard values (typical label ~9-11 g sugar/100 ml; acid estimated). Ginger's pungency is heat: spice on the safe side

lime_cordial.name: lime cordial (commercial, Rose's style)
lime_cordial.source: unsourced standard values (typical label ~28-30 g sugar/100 ml; acid estimated)

irish_whiskey.name: Irish whiskey
irish_whiskey.source: standard bottling strength (Jameson 40%); distilled grain spirit, not gluten (STUDIO-RULES 4)

hot_coffee.name: hot brewed coffee (filter or drip, not espresso)
hot_coffee.source: unsourced standard value: black filter coffee, no sugar; acid small, estimated

hop_syrup.name: hop syrup (1:1 simple syrup steeped with dried hops, strained)
hop_syrup.source: sugar/acid = simple syrup, LI pdf 140-141; hops add aroma only (unsourced). Hops are a flower, not a grain: no gluten; not beer or malt (STUDIO-RULES 4)

scotch_blended_hopped.name: blended scotch whisky, cold-steeped with dried hops (4 g per 250 ml, about 2 hours, strained)
scotch_blended_hopped.source: = blended scotch (LI pdf 140 note, 40% label); hops add aroma only, cold steep, no sugar/acid (unsourced). Distilled grain spirit not gluten; hops are a flower, not beer or malt (STUDIO-RULES 4)

ginger_cumin_syrup.name: cooked ginger and cumin syrup (adapted from the Flavor Matrix Ginger Mule syrup, pdf 135: 10 cm fresh ginger sliced, 480 ml water, 200 g sugar, simmered 5 min; plus 1 tsp cumin seeds toasted dry in the pan first; cooled covered, strained; about 560 ml, fridge)
ginger_cumin_syrup.source: computed from the Matrix recipe: 200 g sugar in ~480 ml water + 124 ml sugar volume (LI 0.62 ml/g) ~ 600 ml, less ~40 ml evaporation over 5 min simmer (unsourced estimate) ~ 560 ml -> ~35.7; rounded down to 34 for ginger solids. Cumin aroma only; cumin is not heat (spice = heat only), but cooked ginger keeps some pungency: spice on the safe side

cocchi_americano.name: Cocchi Americano Bianco (quinquina: white aperitif wine bittered with cinchona)
cocchi_americano.source: ABV 16.5% and sugar 200 g/L: SAQ product page 12433882 (secondary, read by Hester, caregiver-sage round 3). Acid unsourced (as LI's aromatized wines, pp. 136-137, 0.6%). Character: Codex p. 74 (more cinchona bitterness than Lillet). Wine fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4).

suze.name: Suze (French gentian aperitif, 15%)
suze.source: ABV 15%: the flagship (Oxford SUZE pdf 1960; SAQ listing); a 20% Saveur d'Autrefois bottling exists (Oxford pdf 1960), swept. Sugar UNSOURCED estimate 14 g/100 ml, swept 10-18 in the pour's checks. Oxford SUZE pdf 1958: 'predominately flavored with gentian root'. Gentian is a bitter, not heat: no spice (STUDIO-RULES 4).

honey.name: honey (runny, e.g. clover or wildflower)
honey.source: Liquid Intelligence p. 53 (pdf 57): honey 'roughly 82 percent sugar'; x density 1.42 g/ml (unsourced standard value) = ~116 g/100 ml

thyme_sprig.name: fresh thyme sprig
thyme_sprig.source: herb, steeped and removed; no sugar, acid or strength (unsourced standard)

camomile_honey_syrup.name: camomile honey syrup (equal volumes honey and strong hot camomile tea)
camomile_honey_syrup.source: computed, unsourced: honey ~82% sugar, ~1.42 g/ml; 1:1 by volume with tea -> ~58 g/100 ml (LI honey syrup 61.5)

candied_angelica.name: candied angelica stem
candied_angelica.source: garnish served beside the glass, eaten separately; not in the balance. Composition: angelica stem, sugar (glucose syrup, colouring in some brands). Unsourced.

plymouth_gin.name: Plymouth gin (41.2%)
plymouth_gin.source: label ABV 41.2% (unsourced, my knowledge); unsweetened per Oxford PLYMOUTH GIN / GIN pdf 894; angelica in its 1860 seven (Oxford pdf 1538)

jaggery_syrup.name: jaggery syrup (1:1 by weight: grated Indian cane jaggery/gur dissolved in warm water)
jaggery_syrup.source: Hirpara et al., J. Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 9(5) 2020, pp. 3145-3148, Table 1 (Hester's card F19, secondary): solid jaggery 65-85 g sucrose + 9-15 g reducing sugars per 100 g; Hester's hand calculation for 1:1 by weight = ~47-57 g/100 ml (dissolved-volume figure unsourced); row uses 52, swept 47-58 in caregiver-outlaw. Allergens, safe side: makers clarify with chemicals or, for organic jaggery, plant extracts including groundnut and soybean (F20) -> nuts (soy has no veto); milk clarification in some traditional making (Tomás, own knowledge, unsourced, not in F20's list) -> dairy kept until a source rules it out. A vegan label does not rule out groundnut.

rum_indian_old_monk.name: Old Monk 7-year Indian dark rum (recommended; 42.8% in India, 40% in some export markets)
rum_indian_old_monk.source: label ABV; sugar 0 per LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note (any added sugar unsourced, swept)

rum_indian.name: Indian dark rum (style)
rum_indian.source: LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note, 40% typical label; swept 40-45% in caregiver-outlaw

bigallet_china_china.name: Bigallet China-China Amer (40%)
bigallet_china_china.source: ABV 40%: unsourced label value. Sugar UNSOURCED estimate 20 g/100 ml, swept 12-30 in the pour's checks. Codex p. 260: 'between an amaro and a curaçao', crafted with the classic Amer Picon recipe in mind (p. 87). Orange peels and bitter roots: bitters, not heat, so no spice (STUDIO-RULES 4).

pomegranate_syrup.name: pomegranate syrup (equal weights pomegranate juice and sugar, blended cold)
pomegranate_syrup.source: Method: Codex p. 47 House Grenadine (250 g POM juice + 250 g cane sugar), without the malic/citric powders and orange extract. Values computed, unsourced: juice ~14% sugar, ~0.8% acid; 500 g at ~1.25 g/ml = ~400 ml -> ~71 g/100 ml sugar, ~0.5% acid.

rum_navy.name: navy-strength rum (style, 54.5-57%)
rum_navy.source: label ABV, typical navy-strength 57%; historic RN issue 54.5% after 1866 (Oxford RUM, NAVY pdf 1701, Hester F11); sugar 0 per LI pdf 140 straight-spirit note (added sugar unsourced, sweep)

demerara_sherry_vinegar_syrup.name: rich demerara syrup with sherry vinegar (200 g demerara sugar, 100 ml water, warmed until dissolved; off the heat, 30 ml sherry vinegar; about 250 ml, fridge)
demerara_sherry_vinegar_syrup.source: computed: 200 g sugar (demerara treated as sucrose, as LI's demerara syrup 61.9 vs simple 61.5, pdf 140-141) dissolves to ~124 ml (LI 0.62 ml/g) + 100 ml water + 30 ml vinegar = ~254 ml -> 78.7 g/100 ml; sherry vinegar acidity 7% (unsourced: Vinagre de Jerez minimum, own knowledge) -> 2.1 g acetic in 254 ml = 0.83%. Evaporation ignored (warmed, not boiled). Allergens: cane sugar, water, wine vinegar; wine fining ignored (STUDIO-RULES 4); sulphites have no veto.

demerara_sugar_cube.name: brown (demerara) sugar cube
demerara_sugar_cube.source: pure cane sugar; ~4 g per cube as sugar_cube; dissolved volume 0.63 ml per g (unsourced cube weight)
